target.title: refactor: use `node:timers/promises` setTimeout in managed-service handoff script
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removes a hand-written `sleep(ms)` helper in the managed-service update handoff CJS script that re-implements what `node:timers/promises` already provides. The stdlib version has been available since Node.js 16 and OpenClaw already uses it across the codebase (see `src/gateway/`, `src/agents/`, etc.).

## Why This Change Was Made

The handoff script (`HANDOFF_SCRIPT` string literal written to `handoff.cjs`) had its own `sleep` function:
```js
function sleep(ms) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
}
```

This is functionally identical to `const { setTimeout: sleep } = require("node:timers/promises")` but adds unnecessary code that a reviewer has to read and potentially audit. Using the stdlib version is the idiomatic approach and consistent with the rest of the codebase. The change is 1 line added, 3 lines removed.

## User Impact

None. Zero behavioral change.

## Evidence

### Real generated handoff.cjs execution (Node.js v24.13.1)

The handoff script is extracted from the patched `HANDOFF_SCRIPT` string, written to disk as `handoff.cjs` (mode 0o700), and spawned in a real Node.js subprocess — exactly the same execution path as a managed-service handoff:

**Generated script header (patched):**
```js
const { spawn, spawnSync } = require("node:child_process");
const fs = require("node:fs");
const os = require("node:os");
const path = require("node:path");
const { setTimeout: sleep } = require("node:timers/promises");
// ... (no hand-written `function sleep(ms)` — removed)
```

**Execution:**
```
$ node handoff.cjs params.json
(exit code: 0)
```

**Handoff log:**
```
[2026-07-02T11:34:54.056Z] starting managed update command: test
[2026-07-02T11:34:54.062Z] managed update command pid=220865
[2026-07-02T11:34:54.128Z] managed update command exited code=0 signal=null
```

The generated handoff script runs correctly with `node:timers/promises` setTimeout: it starts, waits for the parent to exit, spawns the update command, logs the PID, captures the exit code, and terminates cleanly.

### Unit test output

All existing tests pass with the patched code:

```
$ pnpm test -- src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)

  ✓ starts the managed gateway service when the update command fails after handoff
  ✓ leaves the gateway service alone when the update command succeeds
  ✓ writes a fallback update failure when no restart sentinel row exists
  ✓ sweeps stale handoff temp directories while keeping fresh handoff logs
  ...
```

### CI

70+ CI checks all passing: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99035/checks
